candidates.summary: parseFenceOpener caps the opener's indent at 3 absolute spaces. A list item's fence opened 4-6 spaces in (indent 0-3 from the item's content column) is invisible to the tracker. The item's own closer, written at the content column, then reads to the tracker as an opener, so the item text after it stays unescaped and [home] binds to the realm's definition. This is the third member of the class candidates 8 (HTML block after a list marker) and 9 (tab indent) belong to.

Under CM, goldmark opens the fence at the 5-space line (indent 3 from the item's content column 2) and closes it at the 2-space line, so `see [home]` is a live paragraph in the item and links to the realm's [home]. The 4-space fence under `1. ` is the ordinary way to write code in an ordered list item.
